items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-17 directs the commissioner, after a hearing and written findings, to issue an order requiring the person to cease and desist from the practice, with any penalty ordered.

items.stem: Before the commissioner can order a person to stop an unfair life or annuity trade practice, what must the commissioner first serve on that person?
options: A cease and desist order effective immediately
A notice of a hearing only
A statement of charges and notice of a hearing
A civil complaint filed in Superior Court
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:30-17 requires the commissioner to serve a statement of the charges and a notice of a hearing before any cease and desist order or penalty.

items.stem: Under New Jersey's life insurance disclosure rules, what must an agent tell a prospect before starting a life insurance sales presentation?
options: His commission rate on the proposed policy
His license number and its expiration date
The names of every insurer that has appointed him
That he sells life insurance, and which company he represents
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-11.4(b)-(c) requires the agent to say, prior to commencing a life insurance sales presentation, that he or she is acting as a life insurance agent and to give the full name of the insurer.

items.stem: A New Jersey life producer paid entirely by commissions on policy sales uses business cards reading "Financial Consultant" and describes his business as an advisory practice. He holds no planning designation. Under New Jersey rules, this is:
options: Prohibited, because it implies his pay is unrelated to sales
Permitted, since producers who discuss finances may use the title
Permitted, if he also holds a securities license
Permitted, if the title also appears on the application
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-11.4(b)-(c) bars using terms such as financial planner or financial counseling to imply an advisory business with compensation unrelated to sales unless that is actually the case.

items.stem: Under New Jersey's life insurance disclosure rules, a producer's failure to deliver a required Buyer's Guide is treated as:
options: A clerical error with no penalty
An omission that misrepresents the policy
A breach of contract only
A matter for the insured to raise in court
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-11.5 treats failure to deliver a required Buyer's Guide, policy summary, illustration or policy data as an omission that misrepresents the policy, subject to Unfair Trade Practices Act penalties.

items.stem: A producer uses a basic illustration, and the client applies for the policy exactly as illustrated. Under New Jersey rules, when must the signed illustration be submitted to the insurer?
options: When the policy is delivered
Along with the application
Within 30 days after issue
Only if the insurer requests it
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-52.7 requires a signed copy of the illustration to be submitted to the insurer at the time of application when the policy is applied for as illustrated, with a copy to the applicant.

items.stem: A client applied for a policy as illustrated, but the insurer issues it at a higher rating class. Under New Jersey rules, what must accompany the policy?
options: An amended application signed by the client
A rating letter, with no new illustration
A revised illustration, signed by delivery
The original illustration, marked with the new premium
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-52.7 requires a revised basic illustration labeled "Revised Illustration," conforming to the policy as issued, sent with the policy and signed by the owner and producer no later than delivery.

items.stem: A producer sells a life policy that is marketed with illustrations but shows the client no illustration at all. Under New Jersey rules, the producer must:
options: Do nothing, since showing illustrations is optional
Mail the client an illustration within 30 days
Get the commissioner's approval for the sale
Sign a statement on the company's form saying none was shown
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-52.7 requires the producer to certify in writing, on a form provided by the insurer, that no illustration was used.

items.stem: How long must a New Jersey insurer keep a policy's signed illustration?
options: Until three years after the policy is no longer in force
One year after issue
Five years after issue
Until the policy's next anniversary
items.explanation: N.J.A.C. 11:4-52.7 requires the insurer to retain signed illustrations and related certifications until three years after the policy is no longer in force.

items.stem: A life policy delivered in New Jersey contains a provision less favorable to the policyowner than state law requires. How is the policy interpreted?
options: As written, since the owner accepted it
As void, with all premiums refunded
As written until the commissioner orders a change
As if it complied with the law
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:25-18.1 provides that a policy delivered in New Jersey that does not comply with Title 17B is deemed to comply and is interpreted as if it did, without relieving the insurer of any penalty.

items.stem: An insurer files a new life policy form with the New Jersey commissioner. If the commissioner does not disapprove it in writing, the form is deemed approved after:
options: 30 days
45 days
60 days
90 days
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:25-18.2(b) deems a filed form approved 60 days after submission unless the commissioner disapproves it in writing within that time.

items.stem: A New Jersey insurer delivers a policy that does not comply with Title 17B, so the policy is read as if it complied. What is the effect on the insurer?
options: It is excused from any penalty
It may cancel the policy to cure the violation
It may still be penalized for the violation
It is excused if it reissues the policy
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:25-18.1 reads a noncomplying policy as if it complied, but that does not relieve the insurer from any penalty for the violation.

items.stem: For a policy on another person's life to be valid in New Jersey, when must the beneficiary's insurable interest exist?
options: When the contract is made
When the insured dies
Both at issue and at death
Throughout the life of the policy
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:24-1.1 requires the benefits to be payable to someone who had an insurable interest at the time the contract was made. It need not exist at death.

items.stem: Under New Jersey law, which of the following has an insurable interest in Ana's life without having to show any financial interest in her?
options: Ana's adult sister
Ana's landlord
Ana's next-door neighbor
Ana's former classmate
items.explanation: N.J.S.A. 17B:24-1.1 gives an insurable interest to a person closely related by blood or by law who has a substantial interest engendered by love and affection. Friends, neighbors and coworkers would need a financial interest.

I1-01.statement: Permanent insurance premiums tend to be higher than term premiums because of the savings (cash value) element.
I1-01.citation: NJ DOBI, Consumer Information: Life Insurance
I1-01.quote: Because of the savings element, premiums tend to be higher than term insurance premiums.

I1-02.statement: Universal life, variable universal life and whole life are all forms of permanent insurance.
I1-02.citation: NJ DOBI, Consumer Information: Life Insurance
I1-02.quote: Permanent insurance (such as universal life, variable universal life and whole life) provides long-term financial protection.

I1-03.statement: Whole life covers the insured for life if premiums are paid, generally with the same premium for life.
I1-03.quote: Whole Life Insurance covers you for as long as you live if your premiums are paid. You generally pay the same amount in premiums for as long as you live.

I1-04.statement: A limited-pay whole life policy (for example 20-pay or paid-up at 65) has higher premiums because they are paid over a shorter period.
I1-04.quote: Premiums for these policies are higher since the premium payments are made during a shorter period.

I1-05.statement: Whole life premiums start several times higher than term premiums for the same amount, but are smaller than what renewing term into later years would eventually cost.
I1-05.quote: But they are smaller than the premiums you would eventually pay if you were to keep renewing a term policy until your later years.

I2-01.statement: Unlike other life insurance, variable life has a cash value that varies with the performance of investments the owner chooses, typically mutual funds.
I2-01.quote: Unlike other life insurance, variable life insurance has a cash value that varies depending, in part, on the performance of investments you choose

I2-02.statement: A variable life policyowner can lose money, including the initial investment, if the chosen investments perform poorly.
I2-02.quote: You can lose money in a variable life insurance policy, including potential loss of your initial investment.

I2-10.statement: Universal life lets the owner vary premium payments and adjust the face amount; increases may require proof of insurability.
I2-10.quote: Universal LifeInsurance is a kind of flexible policy that lets you vary your premium payments. You can also adjust the face amount of your coverage. Increases may require proof that you qualify for the new death benefit.

I2-11.statement: If universal life premiums plus interest fall short of the charges, the account value drops, and if it keeps dropping the coverage ends.
I2-11.quote: If your yearly premium payment plus the interest your account earns is less than the charges, your account value will become lower. If it keeps dropping, eventually your coverage will end.

I2-20.statement: Flexible-premium variable (universal) life lets premiums vary as long as they cover fees; if cash value can't cover fees and expenses, the policy may lapse without value.
I2-20.quote: If you do not maintain sufficient cash value to pay your policy’s fees and expenses, your policy may lapse.

I2-21.statement: A variable life death benefit option may equal the face amount, the face amount plus cash value, or the face amount plus premiums paid.
I2-21.quote: the face amount plus the cash value of your account

I2-22.statement: Net amount at risk is the face amount minus the cash value; it falls as the cash value grows.
I2-22.quote: Your net amount of risk is the difference between your policy’s face amount and your policy’s cash value

I2-23.statement: Policy loans reduce cash value, which raises the chance of lapse, and may reduce the death benefit; interest is typically owed.
I2-23.quote: They reduce your policy’s cash value, which increases the likelihood your policy will lapse.

I3-01.statement: Term insurance pays a death benefit only if the insured dies during the term.
I3-01.citation: NJ DOBI, Consumer Information: Life Insurance
I3-01.quote: pays a death benefit only if you die in that term

I3-02.statement: Term insurance generally has lower premiums in the early years but builds no cash value.
I3-02.citation: NJ DOBI, Consumer Information: Life Insurance
I3-02.quote: Term insurance generally has lower premiums in the early years, but does not build up cash values that you can use in the future.

I3-03.statement: Most term policies can be renewed for further terms even if health has changed, but premiums may rise at each renewal.
I3-03.quote: You can renew most term insurance policies for one or more terms even if your health has changed. Each time you renew the policy for a new term, premiums may be higher.

I3-04.statement: Many term policies can be converted to a cash value policy during a conversion period even if the insured is not in good health; the new premium will be higher.
I3-04.quote: You may be able to trade many term insurance policies for a cash value policy during a conversion period - even if you are not in good health.

I3-05.statement: Term insurance generally offers the largest insurance protection for the premium dollar.
I3-05.quote: Term insurance generally offers the largest insurance protection for your premium dollar.

I3-10.statement: If re-entry term requires a new policy at current rates, the whole contract may be contestable for two years and the transaction is treated as a replacement.
I3-10.quote: Such a transaction shall be a replacement and the insurer shall be required to satisfy the requirements of N.J.A.C. 11:4-2.

I4-01.statement: An immediate annuity is bought with a single payment, and income typically starts within one year.
I4-01.quote: With an immediate annuity, you make a single payment to purchase the annuity and typically start receiving income payments within one year of purchase.

I4-03.statement: A fixed annuity guarantees at least a minimum interest rate during accumulation; only the minimum is guaranteed.
I4-03.quote: Fixed annuities guarantee your money will earn at least a minimum interest rate during the accumulation phase.

I4-05.statement: Unlike a fixed indexed annuity, a registered index-linked annuity (RILA) can lose money when the index performs poorly.
I4-05.quote: However, unlike a fixed index annuity, you can lose money in a RILA.

I4-06.statement: A variable annuity lets the owner direct contributions among mutual funds, with no limits on gains or losses.
I4-06.quote: Variable annuities allow you, during the accumulation phase, to direct your contributions to a menu of different mutual funds. There are no limitations on losses or gains

I4-07.statement: Of the four main deferred annuity types, RILAs and variable annuities are securities that must register with the SEC.
I4-07.quote: Of the four main types of deferred annuities shown above, RILAs and variable annuities are securities that must register with the SEC.

I4-08.statement: In a registered MVA annuity, the insurer pays a fixed rate for a period but may adjust contract value, often down, on early withdrawal.
I4-08.quote: In a registered MVA annuity, the insurer pays a fixed rate of interest over a specified period, but may adjust the value of your contract, often down, if you withdraw money early.

I4-09.statement: An insurer's obligations under an annuity depend on its financial strength and claims-paying ability.
I4-09.quote: an insurance company’s obligations under an annuity contract are subject to its financial strength and claims-paying ability

I4-10.statement: Annuities provide tax-deferred growth until income payments begin.
I4-10.quote: Annuities provide: tax-deferred growth until you begin receiving income payments

I4-12.statement: For a RILA, the insurer generally sets parameters that limit both gains and losses.
I4-12.quote: The insurer generally sets parameters that limit both your gains and your losses.

I4-20.statement: A participation rate credits only a percentage of the index gain.
I4-20.quote: if the participation rate is 75% and the index return is calculated to be 10% during the measuring period, the return credited to your annuity would be 7.5%

I4-21.statement: A rate cap is the maximum positive return the contract can earn in a period.
I4-21.quote: The rate cap is a maximum rate of positive return that your contract can earn.

I4-22.statement: A spread (margin or asset fee) subtracts a set percentage from the index gain.
I4-22.quote: This fee subtracts a set percentage from any gain in the index.

I4-23.statement: When features combine, the participation rate is applied first and then the spread is subtracted.

I4-24.statement: Index gains are usually calculated without dividends paid on the index's securities.
I4-24.quote: Any gains in the value of the index are generally calculated without including dividends paid on the securities that make up the index.

I4-25.statement: A floor limits loss to a set percentage; a buffer (shield) absorbs a set percentage of loss before the owner loses value.
I4-25.quote: Buffer or Shield. This protection offers a set percentage of loss that the insurance company is willing to absorb before deducting value from the indexed annuity.

I4-26.statement: With a floor, the owner's loss stops at the floor percentage.
I4-26.quote: This protection limits investor exposure to a set percentage of potential loss.

I4-28.statement: Indexed annuity contracts commonly let the insurer change features like the cap periodically.
I4-28.quote: Indexed annuity contracts commonly allow the insurance company to change some of these features periodically, such as the rate cap.

I4-29.statement: Once annuity income payments begin, the owner generally cannot withdraw money from the account.
I4-29.quote: annuities do not allow you to withdraw money from your account once you have started receiving income payments

I4-30.statement: A common variable annuity death benefit pays the greater of the account value or a guaranteed minimum such as purchase payments minus withdrawals.
I4-30.quote: your beneficiary may receive the greater of: (i) all the money in your account; or (ii) some guaranteed minimum, such as all purchase payments minus prior withdrawals

I4-40.statement: An immediate annuity's premium must be paid in a lump sum, not in installments.
I4-40.quote: shall be paid in a lump sum, and shall not be funded on an installment basis

I4-41.statement: The same contract form may not be issued as both an immediate and a deferred annuity.
I4-41.quote: The same contract form shall not be issued as both an immediate and a deferred annuity.

I5-01.statement: A first-to-die joint policy pays when the first insured dies; it costs less than two individual policies.
I5-01.citation: Alaska Division of Insurance, Life Insurance Considerations
I5-01.quote: A first-to-die policy pays a death benefit when the first person dies.

I5-02.statement: A second-to-die (survivorship) policy pays when the last insured dies and is often bought by married couples to cover federal estate taxes.
I5-02.citation: Alaska Division of Insurance, Life Insurance Considerations
I5-02.quote: Second-or-later-to-die policies are often purchased by married couples who want to protect their assets from federal estate taxes.

I5-10.statement: If only the first insured to die under a survivorship policy commits suicide within the first two years, the insurer generally must reissue it as a single-life policy on the survivor without evidence of insurability.
I5-10.quote: the insurer shall reform and reissue the contract as of the original effective date as a single life contract on the surviving insured

II1-01.statement: Disability and accidental death or dismemberment provisions are excluded from the 2-year incontestable requirement.
II1-01.quote: (exclusive of provisions of the policy or any contract supplemental thereto relating to disability benefits or to additional benefits in event of death by accident or accidental means or in event of dismemberment or loss of sight)

II1-10.statement: A waiver of premium rider lets the owner stop paying premiums if the insured develops a covered illness or disability named in the rider.
II1-10.citation: NAIC Consumer Guide: Life Insurance Riders
II1-10.quote: With a waiver of premium rider, you can stop paying your life insurance premium if you develop a covered illness or disability named in the rider.

II1-11.statement: An accidental death benefit rider pays more than the death benefit, sometimes two or three times (double or triple indemnity), if death is accidental.
II1-11.citation: NAIC Consumer Guide: Life Insurance Riders
II1-11.quote: Some riders pay two to three times the death benefit for certain accidents. Insurers sometimes describe these riders as double or triple indemnity.

II1-12.statement: A guaranteed insurability rider lets the owner increase the death benefit at set future times without a medical exam; the cost depends on age and the amount of the increase, not health.
II1-12.citation: NAIC Consumer Guide: Life Insurance Riders
II1-12.quote: How much it costs to increase the benefit will depend on your age and the amount of the increase, not your health or lifestyle.

II1-13.statement: A long-term care rider lets the insured use part of the death benefit for long-term care, usually triggered by inability to perform certain activities of daily living.
II1-13.citation: NAIC Consumer Guide: Life Insurance Riders
II1-13.quote: Usually, you must be unable to do certain activities of daily living.

II1-14.statement: Money taken under an accelerated death benefit for a terminal illness does not have to be used for care related to the illness.
II1-14.citation: NAIC Consumer Guide: Life Insurance Riders
II1-14.quote: You don't have to use the money to pay for care related to your illness.

II1-20.statement: A rider attaches to a policy to add, subtract or modify coverage and takes precedence over the policy's original provisions.
II1-20.citation: Alaska Division of Insurance, Life Insurance Considerations
II1-20.quote: A rider takes precedence over the original provisions in the policy

II1-21.statement: A family rider provides term insurance on all or certain family members under the insured's policy.
II1-21.citation: Alaska Division of Insurance, Life Insurance Considerations
II1-21.quote: A family rider allows you to provide term insurance on all or certain members of your family under your policy.

II1-22.statement: The guaranteed insurability option may suit someone with a family history of significant medical problems who cannot yet afford a larger death benefit.
II1-22.citation: Alaska Division of Insurance, Life Insurance Considerations
II1-22.quote: This rider may be of value to those with a family history of significant medical problems who currently have limited income and cannot afford a larger death benefit.

II1-30.statement: For coverage on an other insured (such as a spouse or child rider), the form must describe what happens at the primary insured's death; if the coverage ends, unearned premium must be returned or coverage continued for the period paid.
II1-30.quote: If coverage on the other insured terminates upon the death of the primary insured, then the form shall provide for the return of the unearned premium

II1-31.statement: Coverage on an other insured may be continued after the primary insured's death by waiver of premium.
II1-31.quote: The form may continue the coverage on the other insured by waiver of premium

II1-40.statement: A nursing home waiver of annuity surrender charges is limited to confinement of the owner, the annuitant, or the owner's or annuitant's spouse or civil union partner.
II1-40.quote: Confinement of any other family member not identified in the contract shall not qualify for the benefit.

II2-01.statement: An individual life policy must allow a grace period of 30 days, or at the insurer's option one month of at least 30 days.
II2-01.quote: a grace period of 30 days, or, at the option of the insurer, of 1 month of not less than 30 days

II2-02.statement: The policy stays in full force during the grace period, and any unpaid premium may be deducted from a claim that arises during it.
II2-02.quote: during which period of grace the policy shall continue in full force; but if a claim arises under the policy during such period of grace, the amount of any premium due or overdue

II2-03.statement: Interest charged for paying during the grace period may not exceed 6% per year.
II2-03.quote: subject, at the option of the insurer, to an interest charge not in excess of 6% per annum for the number of days of grace

II2-04.statement: The policy becomes incontestable, except for nonpayment of premiums, after it has been in force during the insured's lifetime for 2 years from issue.
II2-04.quote: shall be incontestable, except for nonpayment of premiums, after it has been in force during the lifetime of the insured for a period of 2 years from its date of issue

II2-05.statement: The policy, together with the application if a copy is attached, constitutes the entire contract.
II2-05.quote: the policy, or the policy and the application therefor if a copy of such application is attached to or endorsed upon the policy when issued, shall constitute the entire contract between the parties

II2-06.statement: Absent fraud, statements in the application are representations, not warranties.
II2-06.quote: all statements contained in such an application shall, in the absence of fraud, be deemed representations and not warranties

II2-07.statement: If age is misstated, benefits are what the premium would have bought at the correct age.
II2-07.quote: any amount payable or benefit accruing under the policy shall be such as the premium would have purchased at the correct age or ages

II2-08.statement: Every participating policy must let the dividend be taken in cash, among any other options the policy offers.
II2-08.quote: any dividend credited to the policy shall at the option of the party entitled to elect such option be either: (1) payable in cash, or (2) applied to any one of such other dividend options as may be provided by the policy

II2-09.statement: Participating ordinary policies must apportion divisible surplus annually beginning no later than the end of the third policy year.
II2-09.quote: beginning not later than the end of the third policy year, the insurer shall annually ascertain and apportion the divisible surplus

II2-10.statement: A policy loan must be available once the policy has a cash value and 3 full years' premiums have been paid.
II2-10.quote: after 3 full years' premiums have been paid and after the policy has a cash surrender value

II2-11.statement: The insurer may defer a policy loan for up to 6 months, except a loan to pay a premium to the insurer.
II2-11.quote: The policy shall reserve to the insurer the right to defer the granting of a loan, other than for the payment of any premium to the insurer, for 6 months after application therefor.

II2-12.statement: If loan indebtedness reaches the loan value, the policy terminates only after at least 30 days' mailed notice.
II2-12.quote: the policy shall terminate and become void but not until at least 30 days' notice shall have been mailed by the insurer

II2-13.statement: The required policy loan provision does not apply to term insurance.
II2-13.quote: This section shall not apply to term insurance, or to industrial life insurance policies.

II2-14.statement: A lapsed policy may be reinstated within 3 years of the first unpaid premium's due date, unless surrendered for cash, its values are exhausted, or extended term has expired.
II2-14.quote: the policy will be reinstated at any time within 3 years

II2-15.statement: Reinstatement requires written application, evidence of insurability satisfactory to the insurer, payment of back premiums, and repayment or reinstatement of any policy debt, with interest.
II2-15.quote: upon written application therefor, the production of evidence of insurability satisfactory to the insurer, the payment of all premiums in arrears and the payment or reinstatement of any indebtedness to the insurer upon the policy

II2-16.statement: A reinstated policy can be contested for misstatements in the reinstatement only for the same period, measured from reinstatement, as after original issue.
II2-16.quote: A reinstated policy of life insurance may be contested on account of fraud or misrepresentation of facts material to the reinstatement only for the same period following reinstatement

II2-17.statement: Death claims must be settled within 60 days after receipt of due proof of death.
II2-17.quote: settlement shall be made within 60 days after receipt of due proof of death

II2-18.statement: If a death claim needs more investigation or is denied, the claimant must be told in writing, with the reason, by the 45th day.
II2-18.quote: the claimant shall be notified in writing no later than the 45th calendar day following receipt

II2-19.statement: Overdue death claim payments bear interest at the average return of the State of New Jersey Cash Management Fund.
II2-19.quote: Overdue payments shall bear an annual rate of interest equal to the average rate of return of the State of New Jersey Cash Management Fund

II2-20.statement: After a premium default, the owner may request a paid-up nonforfeiture benefit no later than 60 days after the due date of the premium in default.
II2-20.quote: upon proper request not later than 60 days after the due date of the premium in default, a paid-up nonforfeiture benefit

II2-21.statement: If the owner makes no election within 60 days, the paid-up nonforfeiture benefit specified in the policy takes effect automatically.
II2-21.quote: (3) That a specified paid-up nonforfeiture benefit shall become effective as specified in the policy unless the person entitled to make such election elects another available option

II2-22.statement: For ordinary insurance, a cash surrender value must be available after premiums have been paid for at least 3 full years.
II2-22.quote: after premiums have been paid for at least 3 full years in the case of ordinary insurance

II2-23.statement: If a policy offers dividend options other than cash, it must state which option takes effect automatically when the owner makes no election.
II2-23.quote: the policy shall further state which option shall be automatically effective if such party shall not have elected some other option

II2-24.statement: A life policy may not limit the time to bring a lawsuit to less than 5 years after the cause of action accrues.
II2-24.quote: limits the time within which any action may be commenced to less than 5 years after the cause of action accrues

II2-25.statement: If the policyholder made no settlement agreement, the insurer may hold the proceeds at maturity under an agreement with the beneficiaries.
II2-25.quote: Upon maturity of a policy, in the event the policyholder has made no such agreement, the insurer shall have the power to hold the proceeds of the policy under an agreement with the beneficiaries.

II2-27.statement: Once a policy is paid up, or is continued under a paid-up nonforfeiture benefit that took effect on or after the third anniversary, the insurer must pay the cash surrender value on surrender within 30 days after any policy anniversary.
II2-27.quote: the insurer will pay, upon surrender of the policy within 30 days after any policy anniversary, a cash surrender value

II2-28.statement: Instead of the stipulated paid-up benefit, the insurer may substitute an actuarially equivalent alternative paid-up benefit providing a greater amount or longer period of death benefits.
II2-28.quote: an actuarially equivalent alternative paid-up nonforfeiture benefit which provides a greater amount or longer period of death benefits

II2-40.statement: Under the extended term nonforfeiture option, the policy stays in force as term coverage to a future date; how long depends on the cash value and the insured's age.
II2-40.citation: NC DOI, Standard Policy Provisions and Optional Riders
II2-40.quote: The length of the extended term benefit will depend on the amount of cash value in the policy and the age of the insured.

II2-41.statement: Reduced paid-up insurance uses the cash value to buy a smaller paid-up permanent policy with no further premiums; extended term uses it to buy term insurance.
II2-41.citation: Alaska Division of Insurance, Life Insurance Considerations
II2-41.quote: as reduced paid up insurance - the cash value is used to purchase a paid up permanent life policy (i.e., no premium payments are required)

II2-42.statement: An automatic premium loan pays an overdue premium with a policy loan, preventing lapse if the loan value is enough; the owner usually has to elect it.
II2-42.citation: NC DOI, Standard Policy Provisions and Optional Riders
II2-42.quote: This prevents the policy from lapsing provided the available loan value is sufficient to pay the premium. In most cases the policyowner must choose to enact this provision.

II2-43.statement: Under the interest only settlement option, the insurer keeps the proceeds and pays the beneficiary the interest.
II2-43.citation: Alaska Division of Insurance, Life Insurance Considerations
II2-43.quote: interest only option - insurance company keeps the benefits and provides payment of the interest

II2-44.statement: Under the fixed period option, proceeds are paid out over a set number of months or years; under the fixed amount option, a set amount is paid each period.
II2-44.citation: Alaska Division of Insurance, Life Insurance Considerations
II2-44.quote: fixed period option - benefits are paid out over a predetermined number of months or years

II2-45.statement: The life income settlement option pays benefits for the beneficiary's lifetime.
II2-45.citation: Alaska Division of Insurance, Life Insurance Considerations
II2-45.quote: life income option - benefits are paid for the life of the beneficiary

II2-46.statement: When a premium is paid by automatic premium loan, the insurer must mail written notice showing the loan amount and interest rate within 30 days after the end of the grace period.
II2-46.quote: The notice shall be mailed no later than 30 days after the end of the grace period of the premium paid by loan.

II2-50.statement: A grace-period premium counts as paid on the date the policyholder mails it; the insurer may not require receipt within the grace period and may rely on the postmark.
II2-50.quote: The grace period provision shall not require receipt of the premium by the insurer within the grace period.

II2-51.statement: For account value policies (such as universal life), the grace period is at least 30 days after the policy value hits zero, or at least 60 days after the first monthly deduction date the value cannot cover a full month.
II2-51.quote: (2) No less than 60 days following the first monthly deduction date for which the policy value is insufficient to provide an entire additional month of insurance.

II2-52.statement: The grace period cannot be cut short by terminating the policy for excessive loans; it is in addition to the loan-termination protections.
II2-52.quote: shall not allow the grace period to be preempted by a termination of the policy due to excessive loans

II2-53.statement: The misstatement-of-age provision may not say the policy will be rescinded and premiums refunded; if the true age is outside the issue ages, the insurer extrapolates a premium and benefit.
II2-53.quote: The provision for misstatement of age shall not state that the policy will be rescinded and the premiums refunded.

II2-54.statement: A participating policy must give at least 30 days after a dividend is due to elect a dividend option.
II2-54.quote: no less than 30 days following the date on which the dividend is due and payable

II2-55.statement: A variable policy loan interest rate must be redetermined no less often than every 12 months and no more often than every 3 months.
II2-55.quote: The frequency shall be no less than once every 12 months, but no greater than once every three months.

II2-60.statement: With a variable loan rate, the insurer must notify the policyholder in writing at least 10 days before any rate increase takes effect.
II2-60.quote: Notify the policyholder in writing at least 10 days prior to the effective date of any increase in the interest rate.

II2-61.statement: With a variable loan rate, the insurer must give written notice of the initial rate no later than 30 days after a cash loan.
II2-61.quote: but in no event later than 30 days following the loan

II2-62.statement: If the loan rate is redetermined more often than annually, the policy may not terminate in a policy year solely because of a rate change during that year.
II2-62.quote: the policy shall not terminate in any policy year solely as a result of a change in the interest rate during that year

II2-63.statement: A universal life (account value) policy with a reinstatement provision must offer reinstatement for 3 years from default, and may not charge monthly deductions for the default period beyond the grace period.
II2-63.quote: Monthly deductions cannot be charged for the period of default beyond the grace period.

II2-70.statement: A death claim must be settled within 60 days after the insurer receives due proof of death and any required documents.
II2-70.quote: settlement shall be made within 60 days after receipt of the document or information requested

II2-73.statement: The policy's face-page title must briefly describe the policy, must not mislead, and must state whether it is participating or nonparticipating.
II2-73.quote: shall state if the form is participating or nonparticipating or words of similar meaning

II2-74.statement: Retained asset account funds are not FDIC insured but are guaranteed by the state guaranty associations; the beneficiary can withdraw the entire amount with one draft at any time.
II2-74.quote: are not guaranteed by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), but are guaranteed by the State Guaranty Associations

II2-75.statement: Insurers must give every beneficiary, with the claim form, easy-to-understand information describing all available settlement options.
II2-75.quote: The information shall be provided with the claim form

II3-01.statement: An incontestable clause bars only contests of validity. It does not stop the insurer from relying at any time on exclusions or restrictions in the policy.
II3-01.quote: shall not preclude the assertion at any time of defenses based upon provisions in the policy which exclude or restrict coverage

II3-02.statement: A reinstated policy may carry the same exclusions or restrictions that could have applied at original issue, effective from reinstatement.
II3-02.quote: such reinstated policy may exclude or restrict liability to the same extent that such liability could have been excluded or restricted when the policy was originally issued

II3-10.statement: Under a typical suicide clause, if the insured dies by suicide within the first two years, the insurer pays back the premiums instead of the death benefit.
II3-10.citation: Alaska Division of Insurance, Life Insurance Considerations
II3-10.quote: The insurance company must return premiums paid on the policy.

II3-11.statement: After the suicide exclusion period ends, death by suicide is covered like any other death.
II3-11.citation: NC DOI, Standard Policy Provisions and Optional Riders
II3-11.quote: if a insured commits suicide within the first two years of the insurance contract, the death benefit is limited to the total premiums paid

II3-20.statement: The incontestable and suicide periods start on the earliest of the date of issue, the policy date and any other effective date (except backdating to save age).
II3-20.quote: The periods for incontestability and suicide shall commence upon the earliest of the date of issue, the policy date and any other effective date.

II3-21.statement: When coverage is increased based on new evidence of insurability, the insurer may contest for up to two more years, limited to the increase.
II3-21.quote: the insurer may reserve a right to contest the policy for no more than an additional two years following the date of the purchase of the increase, but only limited to the actual increase in insurance

II3-22.statement: Modifications made without new evidence of insurability, such as cost-of-living or corridor increases, carry no new right to contest.
II3-22.quote: Insurers shall not retain any right of contest when modifications to the policy occur without additional evidence of insurability, such as corridor or cost of living increases.

II3-23.statement: On a conversion or change of plan with no increase in the amount at risk, the suicide period under the new policy runs from the original policy's issue date.
II3-23.quote: the period for death by suicide under the new policy shall begin as of the date of issue of the original policy

II3-31.statement: A military war exclusion may exclude death from war while serving in the armed forces, if death occurs in service or within six months after service ends.
II3-31.quote: provided such death occurs while in such forces or within six months after termination of service in such forces

II3-32.statement: A civilian war exclusion may apply only within two years from the policy's issue date, for death from war while the insured is outside the home area.
II3-32.quote: within two years from the date of issue of the policy, while the insured is not in such forces or units

II3-33.statement: When death results from an excluded act, the insurer must pay at least the greater of premiums paid or the reserve, adjusted for dividends, loans, withdrawals and surrenders.
II3-33.quote: shall be at least equal to the greater of the premiums paid for the policy or the reserve

II3-34.statement: The policyowner must be notified of any war, aviation or avocation exclusion, and a war risk exclusion must be stamped across the face of the policy.
II3-34.quote: the method of notification for a war risk exclusion shall be in the form of a stamp across the face of the policy

II3-35.statement: In New Jersey individual life forms, pre-existing condition exclusions are permitted only for disability benefits.
II3-35.quote: Pre-existing condition exclusions shall only be permitted in the case of benefits for disability

II3-36.statement: A pre-existing condition disclosed on the application but not excluded by rider is covered for disability from the policy's effective date.
II3-36.quote: The insurer shall be liable from the effective date of the policy for a disability resulting from any pre-existing condition which is in an application and not excluded by rider.

III1-01.statement: No one other than the applicant may alter a written application without the applicant's written consent.
III1-01.quote: No alteration on any written application for any such policy or contract shall be made by any person other than the applicant without his written consent

III1-02.statement: The insurer may make insertions for administrative purposes only, marked clearly as not attributable to the applicant.
III1-02.quote: insertions may be made by the insurer, for administrative purposes only, in such manner as to indicate clearly that such insertions are not to be ascribed to the applicant

III1-03.statement: A false statement in the application bars recovery only if it materially affected acceptance of the risk or the hazard assumed.
III1-03.quote: may not bar the right to recovery thereunder unless such false statement materially affected either the acceptance of the risk or the hazard assumed by the insurer

III1-04.statement: An application is admissible as evidence only if a copy was attached to or endorsed on the policy when issued.
III1-04.quote: No application for any life or health insurance policy or annuity contract shall be admissible in evidence in any action relative to such policy or contract, unless a copy of the application was attached to or endorsed upon the policy or contract when issued.

III1-05.statement: On written request after reinstatement or renewal, the insurer must provide a copy of the reinstatement or renewal application within 30 days.
III1-05.quote: the insurer shall, within 30 days after receipt of such request at its home office, deliver or mail to the person making such request a copy of such application

III1-06.statement: A minor at least 15 years old may contract for insurance or annuities on his own life or on someone in whom he has an insurable interest.
III1-06.quote: Any minor not less than 15 years of age may, notwithstanding such minority, contract for annuities or for insurance

III1-07.statement: A minor 15 or older may give a valid receipt for insurance payments totaling up to $2,000 a year, if no guardian has been appointed.
III1-07.quote: As to a minor not less than 15 years of age--a payment or payments in aggregate not exceeding $2,000.00 in any 1 calendar year

III1-20.statement: When replacing a policy, the owner should not cancel the old policy until the new one has been received.
III1-20.quote: If you decide to replace your policy, don't cancel your old policy until you have received the new one.

III1-21.statement: Replacing a policy can be costly, partly because early premiums went to the insurer's selling and issuing costs, which may be paid again on a new policy.
III1-21.quote: Much of what you paid in the early years of the policy you have now paid for the company's cost of selling and issuing the policy. You may pay this type of cost again if you buy a new policy.

III1-30.statement: A producer must submit, with the application, a statement signed by the applicant and producer on whether the applicant has existing policies; if the answer is no, the producer's replacement duties are complete.
III1-30.quote: If the answer is "no," the producer's duties with respect to replacement are complete.

III1-31.statement: If the applicant has existing coverage, the producer must present and offer to read the replacement notice no later than when the application is taken.
III1-31.quote: the producer shall present and offer to read to the applicant, not later than at the time of taking the application, a notice regarding replacements

III1-32.statement: The replacement notice is signed by both the applicant and the producer and stays with the applicant.
III1-32.quote: The notice shall be signed by both the applicant and the producer

III1-33.statement: In a replacement, the producer must give the applicant the original or a copy of all sales material when the application is completed.
III1-33.quote: the producer shall give to the applicant, at the time an application for a new policy or contract is completed, the original or a copy of all sales material

III1-34.statement: The replacing insurer must notify each affected existing insurer within five business days of receiving a completed application indicating replacement.
III1-34.quote: Notify any other existing insurer that may be affected by the proposed replacement within five business days of receipt of a completed application indicating replacement

III1-35.statement: In a replacement, the owner has 30 days from delivery to return the new policy for an unconditional full refund.
III1-35.quote: notice of the right to return the policy or contract within 30 days of the delivery

III1-36.statement: When the replacing insurer is the same as or affiliated with the existing insurer, it must credit the time already elapsed under the old policy's incontestability and suicide periods.
III1-36.quote: the replacing insurer shall allow credit for the period of time that has elapsed under the replaced policy's or contract's incontestability and suicide period

III1-37.statement: On receiving a replacement notification, the existing insurer must tell the owner in writing within five business days of the right to receive information on the existing policy's values.
III1-37.quote: Notify the policy or contract owner in writing within five business days of receipt of a notice referred to in (a)1 above that the policy or contract owner has the right to receive information regarding the existing policy or contract values

III2-01.statement: Written disclosure of an investigative consumer report must be mailed or delivered to the consumer no later than 3 days after the report is first requested.
III2-01.quote: is made in a writing mailed, or otherwise delivered, to the consumer, not later than three days after the date on which the report was first requested

III2-02.statement: On written request, the consumer must be told the nature and scope of the investigation in writing within 5 days.
III2-02.quote: not later than five days after the date on which the request for such disclosure was received from the consumer or such report was first requested, whichever is the later

III2-03.statement: An investigative consumer report includes information on a person's character, general reputation, personal characteristics and mode of living.
III2-03.quote: an investigative consumer report including information as to his character, general reputation, personal characteristics, and mode of living

III2-04.statement: A user that takes adverse action based in whole or part on a consumer report must notify the consumer of the adverse action.
III2-04.quote: If any person takes any adverse action with respect to any consumer that is based in whole or in part on any information contained in a consumer report, the person shall— (1) provide oral, written, or electronic notice of the adverse action to the consumer

III2-05.statement: The adverse action notice must state that the consumer reporting agency did not make the decision and cannot give the specific reasons.
III2-05.quote: a statement that the consumer reporting agency did not make the decision to take the adverse action and is unable to provide the consumer the specific reasons why the adverse action was taken

III2-06.statement: The notice must tell the consumer of the right to a free copy of the report, including the 60-day period for requesting it.
III2-06.quote: which notice shall include an indication of the 60-day period under that section for obtaining such a copy

III2-07.statement: The notice must tell the consumer of the right to dispute the accuracy or completeness of the report with the consumer reporting agency.
III2-07.quote: (B) to dispute, under section 1681i of this title, with a consumer reporting agency the accuracy or completeness of any information in a consumer report furnished by the agency

III2-20.statement: No one may discriminate in issuing or rating life insurance because of race, creed, color, national origin or ancestry.
III2-20.quote: because of race, creed, color, national origin or ancestry

III2-21.statement: Unfair discrimination in life rates is barred between individuals of the same class and equal expectation of life; rating different risk classes differently is allowed.
III2-21.quote: unfair discrimination between individuals of the same class and equal expectation of life

III3-01.statement: An individual life policy must give the policyholder at least 10 days after receiving it to cancel for a prompt refund.
III3-01.quote: during a period of no less than 10 days after the date the policyholder receives the policy

III3-02.statement: The free look period runs from the date the policyholder receives the policy, not the issue date.
III3-02.quote: after the date the policyholder receives the policy

III3-03.statement: A life policy cancelled during the free look gets a prompt refund of all premium paid, including policy fees and other charges.
III3-03.quote: receive from the insurer a prompt refund of any premium paid therefor, including any policy fees or other charges

III3-04.statement: To cancel during the free look, the policyholder mails or otherwise surrenders the policy to the insurer with a written request for cancellation.
III3-04.quote: by mailing or otherwise surrendering the policy to the insurer together with a written request for cancellation

III3-05.statement: Group life insurance is excluded from the individual life free look requirement.
III3-05.quote: No policy of life insurance, other than group insurance,

III3-06.statement: A directly solicited annuity must have a free look of at least 10 days after receipt, with a refund of the account value, including fees and charges.
III3-06.quote: the owner may cancel the annuity and receive from the insurer a prompt refund of any account value of the annuity, including any contract fees or other charges

III3-10.statement: The Buyer's Guide must be given before the insurer accepts the initial premium, unless the policy has an unconditional refund provision of at least 10 days, in which case it may come with the policy.
III3-10.quote: if the policy for which application is made contains an unconditional refund provision of at least 10 days, the Buyer's Guide may be delivered with the policy

III3-11.statement: Without a 10-day unconditional refund provision, the Buyer's Guide must be given before the insurer accepts the applicant's initial premium.
III3-11.quote: prior to accepting the applicant's initial premium or premium deposit

III3-12.statement: On request, policy data for an existing policy is provided for 20 years from the prior anniversary, and the insurer may charge up to $10.
III3-12.quote: The insurer may charge a reasonable fee, not to exceed $ 10.00, for the preparation of the statement

III4-11.statement: No telephone solicitation may be made to a residence before 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m., local time at the called party's location.
III4-11.quote: before the hour of 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m. (local time at the called party's location)

III4-12.statement: A call to a person with whom the caller has an established business relationship is not a telephone solicitation under the do-not-call rules.
III4-12.quote: (ii) To any person with whom the caller has an established business relationship

III4-14.statement: An established business relationship based on a purchase or transaction lasts 18 months.
III4-14.quote: within the eighteen (18) months immediately preceding the date of the telephone call

III4-15.statement: An established business relationship based on an inquiry or application lasts three months.
III4-15.quote: within the three months immediately preceding the date of the call

III4-17.statement: National do-not-call registrations must be honored indefinitely, until cancelled by the consumer or removed by the administrator.
III4-17.quote: Such do-not-call registrations must be honored indefinitely, or until the registration is cancelled by the consumer or the telephone number is removed by the database administrator.

III4-18.statement: When a consumer asks not to be called, the caller must record the request and add the number to its do-not-call list at the time of the request.
III4-18.quote: the person or entity must record the request and place the subscriber's name, if provided, and telephone number on the do-not-call list at the time the request is made

IV1-01.statement: After an assignment, the insurer may deal with the assignee as owner or pledgee until it receives written notice at its home office that the assignment ended.
IV1-01.quote: until the insurer has received at its home office written notice of termination of the assignment or pledge

IV1-02.statement: If the owner alone can change the beneficiary, the policy may be assigned by pledge or by transfer of title through an assignment executed by the owner alone.
IV1-02.quote: may be assigned either by pledge or transfer of title, by an assignment executed by the insured or such owner alone and delivered to the insurer

IV1-11.statement: A person liable for supporting a child or former spouse may buy a policy on that child or former spouse.
IV1-11.quote: An individual liable for the support of a child or former wife or husband may procure a policy of insurance on that child or former wife or husband.

IV1-12.statement: If someone without an insurable interest collects benefits, the insured or his estate may sue to recover those benefits.
IV1-12.quote: the individual insured, or his executor or administrator, as the case may be, may maintain an action to recover those benefits from the person so receiving them

IV1-13.statement: An insurer may rely in good faith on the applicant's statements about insurable interest and is not liable for relying on untrue ones, except as the policy provides.
IV1-13.quote: An insurer shall be entitled to rely upon all statements, declarations and representations made by an applicant for insurance relating to the insurable interest

IV1-14.statement: The insurable interest requirements of 17B:24-1.1 do not apply to group life, group health, blanket insurance or group annuities.
IV1-14.quote: This section shall not apply to group life insurance, group health insurance, blanket insurance or group annuities.

IV2-01.statement: The cost of employer-provided group term life coverage above $50,000 is taxable income to the employee.
IV2-01.quote: the cost of $50,000 of such insurance

IV2-02.statement: The taxable amount of group term coverage is reduced by whatever the employee paid toward it.
IV2-02.quote: the amount (if any) paid by the employee toward the purchase of such insurance

IV2-03.statement: The cost of excess group term coverage is figured from IRS uniform premiums in 5-year age brackets, not the employer's actual premium.
IV2-03.quote: uniform premiums (computed on the basis of 5-year age brackets)

IV2-05.statement: The imputed-income rule does not apply to coverage for any period in which a charity is the sole beneficiary for the entire year.
IV2-05.quote: a person described in section 170(c) is the sole beneficiary

IV3-01.statement: A distribution from a qualified retirement plan before an exception applies is subject to a 10% additional tax on the taxable portion.
IV3-01.quote: increased by an amount equal to 10 percent of the portion of such amount which is includible in gross income

IV3-02.statement: The 10% early distribution tax does not apply to distributions made on or after age 59½.
IV3-02.quote: made on or after the date on which the employee attains age 59½

IV3-03.statement: The 10% early distribution tax does not apply to an employee who separates from service after reaching age 55.
IV3-03.quote: made to an employee after separation from service after attainment of age 55

IV3-04.statement: A Roth IRA distribution is qualified, and tax-free, only if it meets a qualifying event (such as age 59½) and comes after the 5-taxable-year period beginning with the first Roth IRA contribution year.
IV3-04.quote: made within the 5-taxable year period beginning with the first taxable year for which the individual made a contribution to a Roth IRA

IV3-05.statement: For people who reach 72 after 2022 and 73 before 2033, required minimum distributions are based on an applicable age of 73.

IV4-10.statement: Absent an exception, an employer's tax-free death proceeds on employer-owned life insurance are limited to the premiums and other amounts it paid.
IV4-10.quote: shall not exceed an amount equal to the sum of the premiums and other amounts paid by the policyholder for the contract

IV4-11.statement: Employer-owned life insurance proceeds stay fully excludable, if notice and consent were met, when the insured was an employee at any time in the 12 months before death.
IV4-11.quote: was an employee at any time during the 12-month period before the insured’s death

IV4-12.statement: The employee's written notice and consent for employer-owned life insurance must be obtained before the contract is issued.
IV4-12.quote: The notice and consent requirements of this paragraph are met if, before the issuance of the contract, the employee

IV4-13.statement: The written notice must tell the employee the maximum face amount for which he or she could be insured.
IV4-13.quote: the maximum face amount for which the employee could be insured at the time the contract was issued

IV5-01.statement: A worker with 40 quarters of coverage is fully insured for Social Security.

IV5-02.statement: A worker is currently insured with at least 6 quarters of coverage in the 13-quarter period ending with the quarter of death or entitlement.
IV5-02.quote: not less than six quarters of coverage during the thirteen-quarter period

IV5-03.statement: For anyone who reaches early retirement age (62) after 2021, Social Security full retirement age is 67.
IV5-03.quote: (E) with respect to an individual who attains early retirement age after December 31, 2021, 67 years of age.

IV5-04.statement: Early retirement age for a worker's own old-age benefit is 62 (60 for a widow's or widower's benefit).
IV5-04.quote: The term “early retirement age” means age 62 in the case of an old-age, wife’s, or husband’s insurance benefit, and age 60 in the case of a widow’s

IV6-01.statement: Life insurance proceeds paid by reason of the insured's death are generally excluded from gross income.
IV6-01.quote: gross income does not include amounts received (whether in a single sum or otherwise) under a life insurance contract, if such amounts are paid by reason of the death of the insured

IV6-02.statement: If a policy is transferred for valuable consideration, the exclusion is limited to the consideration paid plus later premiums paid by the transferee.
IV6-02.quote: the amount excluded from gross income by paragraph (1) shall not exceed an amount equal to the sum of the actual value of such consideration and the premiums and other amounts subsequently paid by the transferee

IV6-03.statement: Exchanging a life insurance contract for another life contract, an endowment, an annuity or a qualified long-term care contract recognizes no gain or loss.
IV6-03.quote: (1) a contract of life insurance for another contract of life insurance or for an endowment or annuity contract or for a qualified long-term care insurance contract

IV6-04.statement: An annuity may be exchanged without recognizing gain only for another annuity or a qualified long-term care contract.
IV6-04.quote: (3) an annuity contract for an annuity contract or for a qualified long-term care insurance contract

IV6-05.statement: A taxable distribution from an annuity is generally subject to an additional 10% tax on the portion included in gross income.
IV6-05.quote: increased by an amount equal to 10 percent of the portion of such amount which is includible in gross income

IV6-06.statement: The 10% penalty does not apply to annuity distributions made on or after age 59½.
IV6-06.quote: (A) made on or after the date on which the taxpayer attains age 59½,

IV6-07.statement: A contract entered into on or after June 21, 1988 that fails the 7-pay test is a modified endowment contract.
IV6-07.quote: (A) is entered into on or after June 21, 1988, and (B) fails to meet the 7-pay test of subsection (b)

IV6-08.statement: A contract received in exchange for a modified endowment contract is also a modified endowment contract.
IV6-08.quote: (2) which is received in exchange for a contract described in paragraph (1) or this paragraph.

IV6-09.statement: No deduction is allowed for premiums on a life insurance policy, endowment or annuity if the taxpayer is directly or indirectly a beneficiary.
IV6-09.quote: Premiums on any life insurance policy, or endowment or annuity contract, if the taxpayer is directly or indirectly a beneficiary under the policy or contract.

IV6-10.statement: The 10% penalty does not apply to annuity distributions made on or after the holder's death, or attributable to the taxpayer becoming disabled.
IV6-10.quote: (B) made on or after the death of the holder

IV7-01.statement: Amounts received under a life insurance contract on the life of a terminally ill insured are treated as paid by reason of death.
IV7-01.quote: (A) Any amount received under a life insurance contract on the life of an insured who is a terminally ill individual.

IV7-02.statement: Amounts received on the life of a chronically ill insured are also treated as paid by reason of death.
IV7-02.quote: (B) Any amount received under a life insurance contract on the life of an insured who is a chronically ill individual.

IV7-10.statement: In a viatical settlement, the owner (viator) sells the policy to a third party, the provider, who becomes the owner, pays the premiums and collects the death benefit.
IV7-10.citation: Alaska Division of Insurance, Life Insurance Considerations
IV7-10.quote: The buyer (the viatical settlement provider) becomes the new owner of the life insurance policy, pays future premiums, and collects the death benefit when the insured dies.

IV7-20.statement: A New Jersey accelerated death benefit's terminal-illness trigger must define a drastically limited life span of no less than 6 months and no more than 24 months, as specified in the policy.
IV7-20.quote: shall have a minimum of "six months or less" and a maximum of "24 months or less" and shall be specified in the policy

IV7-21.statement: Accelerated death benefits are paid to the owner during the insured's lifetime and reduce the death benefit otherwise payable.
IV7-21.quote: That reduces the death benefit otherwise payable under the policy or certificate

IV7-23.statement: New Jersey permits accelerated death benefits only in two forms: a surrender of the policy or a lien on the death benefits.
IV7-23.quote: either a surrender of the policy or a lien on the death benefits

IV7-24.statement: Under the surrender approach, the cash value is reduced by the same percentage as the death benefit.
IV7-24.quote: the cash value, if any, is reduced by the same percentage as the death benefit

IV7-25.statement: Under the surrender approach, the accelerated amount may repay a policy loan only up to the loan multiplied by the percentage of death benefit accelerated.
IV7-25.quote: but only up to the amount of the outstanding loan multiplied by the percentage of the death benefits which have been accelerated

IV7-26.statement: Under the surrender approach, the premium is proportionately reduced to reflect the insurance remaining in force.
IV7-26.quote: The premium is proportionately reduced to reflect the amount of insurance remaining in effect

IV8-01.statement: For the federal definition of life insurance, a contract's maturity date is deemed to be no earlier than age 95 and no later than age 100.
IV8-01.quote: shall be deemed to be no earlier than the day on which the insured attains age 95, and no later than the day on which the insured attains age 100

IV8-02.statement: For the federal tests, an endowment benefit is deemed not to exceed the smallest death benefit payable under the contract.
IV8-02.quote: shall be deemed not to exceed the least amount payable as a death benefit at any time under the contract

IV8-03.statement: A contract qualifies as life insurance for tax purposes only if it meets the cash value accumulation test, or the guideline premium requirements plus the cash value corridor.
IV8-03.quote: meets the guideline premium requirements of subsection (c), and (B) falls within the cash value corridor

IV8-04.statement: If a contract fails the federal definition of life insurance, the income on the contract each year is taxed to the policyholder as ordinary income.
IV8-04.quote: the income on the contract for any taxable year of the policyholder shall be treated as ordinary income

IV8-05.statement: Under New Jersey law, life insurance includes the granting of endowment benefits.
IV8-05.quote: Life insurance includes also the granting of endowment benefits

V1-02.statement: No one may solicit, negotiate or effect insurance, deliver a policy, collect premiums or otherwise transact insurance in New Jersey unless specifically authorized.
V1-02.quote: unless specifically authorized under the laws of this State

V1-03.statement: Every insurer must file a sworn annual financial statement with the commissioner by March 1, and quarterly statements within 45 days after each quarter.
V1-03.quote: on or before March 1, file with the commissioner a statement subscribed and sworn to

V2-01.statement: A domestic insurer is one formed under New Jersey law.
V2-01.quote: A “domestic” insurer is one formed under the laws of this State.

V2-02.statement: A foreign insurer is one formed under the laws of another U.S. jurisdiction.
V2-02.quote: A “foreign” insurer is one formed under the laws of a jurisdiction of the United States of America other than this State.

V2-03.statement: An alien insurer is one formed under the laws of a country other than the United States.
V2-03.quote: An “alien” insurer is one formed under the laws of any country other than the United States of America

V2-04.statement: Life insurance as defined in New Jersey includes accidental death and dismemberment benefits and disability waiver-type provisions added to a life policy.
V2-04.quote: additional benefits in event of death by accident or accidental means or in event of dismemberment or loss of sight

V2-05.statement: A contract with life or health extras is still an annuity if those extras are a subsidiary or incidental part of the contract.
V2-05.quote: shall nevertheless be deemed to be an annuity if such extra benefits constitute a subsidiary or incidental part of the entire contract

V2-06.statement: A certificate of authority evidences an insurer's authority to transact insurance; a license authorizes a person to act as an agent, broker or solicitor.
V2-06.quote: A “certificate of authority” is a certificate issued by the commissioner evidencing the authority of an insurer to transact insurance in this State.

V3-01.statement: A person may not sell, solicit or negotiate insurance in New Jersey unless licensed for that line of authority.
V3-01.quote: A person shall not sell, solicit or negotiate insurance in this State unless the person is licensed for that line of authority in accordance with this act.

V3-02.statement: A resident individual applying for a producer license must pass a written examination unless exempt.
V3-02.quote: A resident individual applying for an insurance producer license shall pass a written examination unless exempt

V3-03.statement: The examination tests the lines of authority applied for, a producer's duties and responsibilities, and New Jersey insurance laws and regulations.
V3-03.quote: The examination shall test the knowledge of the individual concerning the lines of authority for which application is made, the duties and responsibilities of an insurance producer and the insurance laws and regulations of this State.

V3-04.quote: Each individual applying for an examination shall remit a nonrefundable fee

V3-05.statement: An applicant who misses or fails the exam may reapply but must remit all required fees and forms again before being rescheduled.
V3-05.quote: may reapply for an examination and shall remit all required fees and forms before being rescheduled for another examination

V3-06.statement: The examination and its registration materials must be offered in English and Spanish.
V3-06.quote: the examination and registration materials for the examination shall be offered in English and Spanish

V3-07.statement: A resident individual applicant must be at least 18 years of age.
V3-07.quote: (1) Is at least 18 years of age;

V3-08.statement: A resident individual applicant must complete a prelicensing course of study for the lines of authority applied for.
V3-08.quote: Has completed a prelicensing course of study for the lines of authority for which the individual has applied

V3-09.statement: A business entity seeking a producer license must designate a licensed producer responsible for the entity's compliance with New Jersey insurance law.
V3-09.quote: The business entity has designated a licensed insurance producer or producers responsible for the business entity's compliance

V3-10.statement: Applicants submit fingerprints and written consent for a criminal history record background check, and the applicant bears its cost.
V3-10.quote: The applicant shall bear the cost for the criminal history record background check

V3-11.statement: Applicants must submit fingerprints and written consent for a criminal history record background check.
V3-11.quote: shall submit to the commissioner the applicant's name, address, fingerprints and written consent for a criminal history record background check to be performed

V3-12.statement: The life line of authority covers insurance on human lives, including endowment and annuity benefits.
V3-12.quote: (1) Life-insurance coverage on human lives, including benefits of endowment and annuities

V3-13.statement: Variable life and variable annuity products, which reflect the investment experience of a separate account, are a separate line of authority.
V3-13.quote: (5) Variable life and variable annuity products-insurance coverage provided under variable life insurance contracts, variable annuities or any other life insurance or annuity product that reflects the investment experience of a separate account

V3-14.statement: The personal lines line of authority covers property and casualty insurance sold to individuals and families for primarily noncommercial purposes.
V3-14.quote: (7) Personal lines--property and casualty insurance coverage sold to individuals and families for primarily noncommercial purposes

V3-15.statement: A license remains in effect unless revoked or suspended as long as the fee is paid on time and, for resident individuals, education requirements are met on time.
V3-15.quote: is timely paid and in the case of resident individual insurance producers, education requirements are timely satisfied

V3-16.statement: A lapsed individual license may be reinstated within 12 months of the renewal fee due date without retaking the exam.
V3-16.quote: may, within 12 months from the due date of the renewal fee, reinstate the same license without the necessity of passing a written examination

V3-17.statement: A renewal fee received after the due date carries a penalty of up to double the unpaid renewal fee.
V3-17.quote: a penalty in an amount not to exceed double the unpaid renewal fee

V3-18.statement: A producer unable to renew because of military service or another extenuating circumstance, such as long-term medical disability, may request a waiver of renewal procedures.
V3-18.quote: unable to comply with license renewal procedures due to military service or some other extenuating circumstance, such as long-term medical disability, may request a waiver

V3-19.statement: Licensees must inform the commissioner of a change of address within 30 days.
V3-19.quote: Licensees shall inform the commissioner by any means acceptable to the commissioner of a change of address within 30 days of the change.

V3-20.statement: A nonresident license requires being currently licensed as a resident producer in good standing in the home state.
V3-20.quote: (1) The person is currently licensed as a resident insurance producer in good standing in his home state;

V3-21.statement: New Jersey grants a nonresident license only if the applicant's home state licenses New Jersey residents on the same basis.
V3-21.quote: (4) The person's home state awards nonresident insurance producer licenses to residents of this State on the same basis.

V3-22.statement: A licensed nonresident producer is deemed to have appointed the commissioner as agent to receive service of legal process in New Jersey.
V3-22.quote: be deemed to have appointed the commissioner as agent to receive service of original legal process in this State

V3-23.statement: A resident producer who moves from New Jersey to another state must file a change of address and certification from the new state within 30 days, with no fee or application.
V3-23.quote: shall file a change of address and provide certification from the new resident state within 30 days of the change of legal residence. No fee or license application shall be required.

V3-24.statement: A producer previously licensed in another state is exempt from prelicensing education and the exam if currently licensed there or if the application is received within 90 days of cancellation, with proof of good standing.
V3-24.quote: if the application is received within 90 days of the cancellation of the applicant's previous license

V3-25.statement: A producer licensed in another state who moves to New Jersey must apply for a resident license within 90 days of establishing legal residence.
V3-25.quote: shall make application within 90 days of establishing legal residence to become a resident licensee

V3-26.statement: A producer who moves to New Jersey needs no prelicensing education or exam for lines already held in the prior state, unless a regulation provides otherwise.
V3-26.quote: No prelicensing education or examination shall be required of that person to obtain any lines of authority previously held in the prior state except in cases in which the commissioner determines otherwise by regulation.

V3-27.statement: A producer doing business under a name other than the legal name must notify the commissioner before using the assumed name.
V3-27.quote: An insurance producer doing business under any name other than the producer's legal name shall notify the commissioner prior to using the assumed name.

V3-28.statement: A temporary producer license may be issued without an exam for no more than 180 days.
V3-28.quote: a temporary insurance producer license for a period not to exceed 180 days without requiring an examination

V3-29.statement: A temporary license may go to the surviving spouse or court-appointed personal representative of a producer who dies or becomes disabled.
V3-29.quote: (1) To the surviving spouse or court-appointed personal representative of a licensed insurance producer, upon the death or disability of that producer

V3-30.statement: A temporary license may go to the designee of a producer entering active military service.
V3-30.quote: (3) To the designee of a licensed insurance producer entering active service in the armed forces of the United States of America;

V3-31.statement: The commissioner may require a temporary licensee to have a sponsor who is a licensed producer or insurer and assumes responsibility for the licensee's acts.
V3-31.quote: The commissioner may require the temporary licensee to have a suitable sponsor who is a licensed insurance producer or insurer and who assumes responsibility for all acts of the temporary licensee

V3-32.statement: Improperly using notes or other reference material to complete the licensing exam is a ground for license action.
V3-32.quote: (11) Improperly using notes or any other reference material to complete an examination for an insurance producer license;

V3-33.statement: Conviction of a felony or a crime of the fourth degree or higher is a ground for license action.
V3-33.quote: (6) Having been convicted of a felony or crime of the fourth degree or higher;

V3-34.statement: Failing to comply with an administrative or court order imposing a child support obligation is a ground for license action.
V3-34.quote: (13) Failing to comply with an administrative or court order imposing a child support obligation;

V3-35.statement: Failing to notify the commissioner within 30 days of a conviction, indictment or the filing of formal criminal charges is a ground for license action.
V3-35.quote: (18) Failing to notify the commissioner within 30 days of his conviction of any crime, indictment or the filing of any formal criminal charges

V3-36.statement: When a license is denied or not renewed, the commissioner must give the reason in writing, and the applicant or licensee may demand a hearing.
V3-36.quote: advise, in writing, the applicant or licensee of the reason for the denial or nonrenewal of the license. The applicant or licensee may make written demand upon the commissioner for a hearing

V3-37.statement: A business entity's license may be suspended, revoked or refused if its partners, officers or managers knew or should have known of a producer's violation and neither reported nor corrected it.
V3-37.quote: an individual licensee's violation was known or should have been known by one or more of the partners, officers or managers acting on behalf of the business entity and the violation was neither reported to the commissioner nor corrective action taken

V3-38.statement: The commissioner keeps enforcement authority over a person under investigation even if the license was surrendered or lapsed.
V3-38.quote: even if the person's license or registration has been surrendered or has lapsed by operation of law
