V3-39.statement: An insurer or producer may not pay a commission to a person who must be licensed and is not.
V3-39.quote: An insurer or insurance producer shall not pay a commission, service fee, brokerage or other valuable consideration to a person for selling, soliciting or negotiating insurance in this State if that person is required to be licensed under this act and is not so licensed.

V3-40.statement: Renewal or deferred commissions may be paid to a person who was licensed at the time of the sale.
V3-40.quote: Renewal or other deferred commissions may be paid to a person for selling, soliciting or negotiating insurance in this State if the person was required to be licensed under this act at the time of the sale, solicitation or negotiation and was so licensed at that time.

V3-41.statement: A producer must report administrative action taken in another jurisdiction, or by another New Jersey agency, within 30 days of final disposition.
V3-41.quote: shall report to the commissioner any administrative action taken against the insurance producer in another jurisdiction or by another governmental agency in this State within 30 days of the final disposition of the matter

V3-42.statement: A producer's report of a criminal prosecution must include a copy of the initial complaint, the order resulting from the hearing and other relevant legal documents.
V3-42.quote: The report shall include a copy of the initial complaint filed, the order resulting from the hearing and any other relevant legal documents.

V3-43.statement: An insurer or producer may pay a fee to persons who do not sell, solicit or negotiate insurance, unless the payment would violate another law such as the rebating rules.
V3-43.quote: An insurer or insurance producer may pay or assign commissions, service fees, brokerages or other valuable consideration to an insurance agency or to persons who do not sell, solicit or negotiate insurance in this State

V4-01.statement: Misrepresenting policy terms or benefits, or misrepresenting to induce a policyholder to lapse, forfeit or surrender, is an unfair practice.
V4-01.quote: making any misrepresentation to any policyholder insured in any company for the purpose of inducing or tending to induce such policyholder to lapse, forfeit, or surrender his insurance

V4-02.statement: Advertising or statements about the business of insurance that are untrue, deceptive or misleading are prohibited.
V4-02.quote: an advertisement, announcement or statement containing any assertion, representation or statement with respect to the business of insurance or with respect to any person in the conduct of his insurance business, which is untrue, deceptive or misleading

V4-03.statement: Defamation is a false or maliciously critical statement about an insurer's financial condition calculated to injure someone in the insurance business.
V4-03.quote: which is false, or maliciously critical of or derogatory to the financial condition of an insurer, and which is calculated to injure any person engaged in the business of insurance

V4-04.statement: Boycott, coercion or intimidation that restrains or monopolizes the business of insurance is an unfair practice.
V4-04.quote: any act of boycott, coercion or intimidation resulting in or tending to result in unreasonable restraint of, or monopoly in, the business of insurance

V4-05.statement: Unfair discrimination in life insurance rates between individuals of the same class and equal expectation of life is prohibited.
V4-05.quote: any unfair discrimination between individuals of the same class and equal expectation of life in the rates charged for any contract of life insurance

V4-06.statement: Discrimination because of race, creed, color, national origin or ancestry in issuing, withholding, extending or renewing any policy is prohibited.
V4-06.quote: because of race, creed, color, national origin or ancestry of such person or group of persons in the issuance, withholding, extension or renewal of any policy of insurance

V4-07.statement: Giving a rebate of premium, or any valuable consideration not specified in the contract, as an inducement to buy life, annuity or health insurance is a prohibited rebate.
V4-07.quote: any rebate of premiums payable on the contract, or any special favor or advantage in the dividends or other benefits thereon, or any valuable consideration or inducement whatsoever not specified in the contract

V4-08.statement: Fair and equitable bonuses or premium abatements paid to policyholders out of surplus from nonparticipating insurance are not rebates or unfair discrimination.
V4-08.quote: paying bonuses to policyholders or otherwise abating their premiums in whole or in part out of surplus accumulated from nonparticipating insurance; provided, that any such bonuses or abatement of premiums shall be fair and equitable to policyholders

V4-09.statement: Readjusting a group policy's premium rate on loss or expense experience at the end of a policy year is permitted, retroactive only for that policy year.
V4-09.quote: readjustment of the rate of premium for a group policy based on the loss or expense experience thereunder, at the end of the first or any subsequent policy year of insurance thereunder, which may be made retroactive only for such policy year

V4-10.statement: Improper claim handling is an unfair claim settlement practice when committed with such frequency as to indicate a general business practice.
V4-10.quote: Committing or performing with such frequency as to indicate a general business practice any of the following

V4-12.statement: Paying claims without a statement of the coverage under which payment is made is an unfair claim settlement practice.
V4-12.quote: (j) Making claims payments to insureds or beneficiaries not accompanied by a statement setting forth the coverage under which the payments are being made;

V4-13.statement: An insurer must keep a complete record of all complaints received since its last examination.
V4-13.quote: Failure of any person to maintain a complete record of all the complaints which it has received since the date of its last examination.

V4-14.statement: For the complaint record, a complaint is any written communication primarily expressing a grievance.
V4-14.quote: “complaint” shall mean any written communication primarily expressing a grievance

V4-15.statement: An insurer's complaint record must show the total number of complaints, their classification by line, the nature and disposition of each, and the time taken to process each.
V4-15.quote: This record shall indicate the total number of complaints, their classification by line of insurance, the nature of each complaint, the disposition of these complaints, and the time it took to process each complaint.

V4-30.statement: Lower rates for policies on payroll deduction, bank draft or similar plans are not unfair discrimination if reasonably related to the savings from the plan.
V4-30.quote: such rate or underwriting considerations being reasonably related to the savings made by the use of such plan

V4-40.statement: The ban on rebates and inducements applies whether or not a policy is ultimately issued.
V4-40.quote: The provisions of this section shall apply whether or not a contract of insurance is ultimately effected.

V4-42.statement: Twisting is a misleading representation or incomplete or fraudulent comparison of policies or insurers to induce someone to lapse, surrender or replace a policy.
V4-42.quote: make any misleading representations or incomplete or fraudulent comparison of any insurance policies or annuity contracts or insurers

V4-50.statement: A policy may not provide credits for a surrender charge imposed under another contract, since that unfairly discriminates based on the source of funding.
V4-50.quote: A policy shall not provide credits for a surrender charge imposed under another contract

V4-63.statement: Civil penalties under the Insurance Fraud Prevention Act are up to $5,000 for a first violation, $10,000 for a second and $15,000 for each subsequent violation.
V4-63.quote: $5,000 for the first violation, $10,000 for the second violation and $15,000 for each subsequent violation

V4-64.statement: Anyone who believes the Insurance Fraud Prevention Act has been violated must notify the bureau and the Office of the Insurance Fraud Prosecutor immediately after discovery.
V4-64.quote: shall notify the bureau and the Office of the Insurance Fraud Prosecutor immediately after discovery of the alleged violation

V5-01.statement: Every member insurer must belong to the association as a condition of its authority to do business in New Jersey.
V5-01.quote: All member insurers shall be and remain members of the association as a condition of their authority or license to transact insurance

V5-02.statement: An insurer remains a member for four years after it stops holding a certificate of authority or license.
V5-02.quote: Any member insurer shall remain a member insurer for four years after it ceases to hold a certificate of authority or license.

V5-03.statement: The association keeps two accounts: a life insurance and annuity account, and a health account.
V5-03.quote: (1) The life insurance and annuity account which shall include the following subaccounts: (a) life insurance subaccount; (b) annuity subaccount; and (c) unallocated annuity subaccount. (2) The health account.

V5-04.statement: For one life, the association's limit for life insurance death benefits is $500,000, regardless of the number of policies.
V5-04.quote: with respect to one life, regardless of the number of policies or contracts: (a) $500,000 in life insurance death benefits

V5-05.statement: For life insurance, net cash surrender and withdrawal values are limited to $100,000 per life.
V5-05.quote: but not more than $100,000 in net cash surrender and net cash withdrawal values for life insurance

V5-06.statement: For annuities, net cash surrender and withdrawal values are limited to $250,000 per life.
V5-06.quote: but not more than $250,000 in net cash surrender and net cash withdrawal values for annuity benefits

V5-07.statement: The association will not spend more than $500,000 in the aggregate for any one individual's life and annuity benefits.
V5-07.quote: in no event shall the association be liable to expend more than $500,000 in the aggregate with respect to any one individual under this paragraph (2)

V5-08.statement: The limit for any one unallocated annuity contract is $2,000,000.
V5-08.quote: (3) with respect to any one unallocated annuity contract, $2,000,000 in benefits

V5-09.statement: For accident or health insurance policies, the New Jersey act provides unlimited benefits.
V5-09.quote: (4) with respect to any one group, blanket, or individual accident or health insurance or group, blanket or individual accident or health insurance policy, unlimited benefits

V5-10.statement: No insurer, producer or agent may use the existence of the association to sell, solicit or induce a purchase.
V5-10.quote: which uses the existence of the association for the purpose of sales, solicitation, or inducement to purchase any form of insurance

V5-11.statement: A member insurer must deliver the association's summary document to the policyowner prior to or at the time the policy is delivered.
V5-11.quote: unless the document is delivered to the policy or contract owner, certificate holder, or enrollee prior to or at the time of delivery of the policy or contract

V5-12.statement: The summary document's disclaimer must warn that the association may not cover the policy, and that any coverage is subject to limitations and conditioned on continued residence in New Jersey.
V5-12.quote: the association may not cover the policy or contract or, if coverage is available, it will be subject to substantial limitations and exclusions and conditioned on continued residence in this State

V6-01.statement: A New Jersey insurance producer acts in a fiduciary capacity in conducting insurance business.
V6-01.quote: An insurance producer acts in a fiduciary capacity

V6-03.statement: Premium funds must be remitted to the insurer within five business days of receipt, unless a contract, agreement or controlling rule provides otherwise.
V6-03.quote: within five business days after receipt of the funds

V6-04.statement: Return premiums due the insured must be paid or credited within five business days after the producer receives them.
V6-04.quote: All premiums due the insured shall be paid to the insured or credited to the insured's account within five business days

V6-05.statement: Policies received for delivery must be delivered or mailed to the insured within 10 calendar days, unless the insured agrees in writing to a longer retention.
V6-05.quote: within 10 calendar days of their receipt by the insurance producer, unless the insured agrees in writing

V6-06.statement: A producer must witness the applicant's signature only when the application was completed in a face-to-face meeting; the insurer may waive this in writing in advance.
V6-06.quote: only when the application is signed by the applicant after having been completed in a face to face meeting

V6-07.statement: Within 10 days after a transaction modifying a contract or application, the producer must confirm in writing the information the client submitted and that it was sent to the insurer.
V6-07.quote: within 10 days after the effectuation of an insurance transaction made through an insurance producer which modifies the terms of an existing insurance contract

VI1-01.statement: Credit life insurance is insurance on a debtor's life in connection with a specific loan or credit transaction.
VI1-01.quote: means insurance on the life of a debtor pursuant to or in connection with a specific loan or other credit transaction

VI1-02.statement: Credit life insurance may be issued only on the term plan, as individual policies to debtors or group policies to creditors.
VI1-02.quote: Individual policies of life insurance issued to debtors on the term plan

VI1-03.statement: Credit life coverage may not exceed the total amount repayable, and on installment debt may not exceed the greater of the scheduled or actual unpaid balance.
VI1-03.quote: The initial amount of credit life insurance shall not exceed the total amount repayable under the contract of indebtedness

VI1-04.statement: Credit insurance may not run more than 15 days past the debt's scheduled maturity unless extended at no extra cost to the debtor.
VI1-04.quote: The term of such insurance shall not extend more than 15 days beyond the scheduled maturity date of the indebtedness except when extended without additional cost to the debtor.

VI1-05.statement: Credit insurance benefits go to the creditor to reduce or pay off the debt; any excess goes to a beneficiary named by the debtor (not the creditor) or the debtor's estate.
VI1-05.quote: any such excess shall be payable to a beneficiary, other than the creditor, named by the debtor or to his estate

VI1-07.statement: The amount charged to a debtor for credit insurance may not exceed the premium the insurer charges.
VI1-07.quote: shall not exceed the premiums charged by the insurer, as computed at the time the charge to the debtor is determined

VI2-01.statement: A group life policy must give the policyholder a 31-day grace period for premiums after the first, with death benefit coverage continuing during it.
VI2-01.quote: entitled to a grace period of 31 days for the payment of any premium due except the first

VI2-02.statement: A New Jersey group life policy becomes incontestable, except for nonpayment, after it has been in force for two years from issue.
VI2-02.quote: the validity of the policy shall not be contested except for nonpayment of premiums after it has been in force for two years from its date of issue

VI2-03.statement: When group coverage ends because employment or eligible membership ends, the person may convert to an individual policy without evidence of insurability by applying and paying the first premium within 31 days.
VI2-03.quote: without evidence of insurability, an individual policy of life insurance without disability or other supplementary benefits, provided application for the individual policy shall be made, and the first premium paid to the insurer, within 31 days after termination

VI2-04.statement: The converted policy's premium is the insurer's customary rate for the form, amount, risk class and the person's attained age when the individual policy takes effect.
VI2-04.quote: (3) The premium on the individual policy shall be at the insurer's then customary rate applicable to the form and amount of the individual policy, to the class of risk to which the person then belongs, and to the individual age attained on the effective date of the individual policy.

VI2-05.statement: The converted policy may not exceed the amount of group life insurance that ended, less any new group coverage the person becomes eligible for within 31 days.
VI2-05.quote: (2) The individual policy shall be in an amount not in excess of the amount of life insurance that ceases because of termination

VI2-06.statement: If a person is not told of the conversion right at least 15 days before the period ends, the period extends to 15 days after notice, but never more than 60 days past the original deadline.
VI2-06.quote: This additional period shall expire 15 days after the individual is given notice but in no event shall the additional period extend beyond 60 days after the expiration date of the period provided in the policy.

VI3-01.statement: Misleading representations or incomplete or fraudulent comparisons made to induce someone to lapse, surrender, terminate, retain or convert a policy or annuity are prohibited (twisting).
VI3-01.quote: No person shall make any misleading representations or incomplete or fraudulent comparison of any insurance policies or annuity contracts or insurers for the purpose of inducing, or tending to induce, any person to lapse, forfeit, surrender, terminate, retain, or convert any insurance policy or annuity contract

VI3-02.statement: Making false or misleading statements about dividends or surplus previously paid on similar policies is prohibited.
VI3-02.quote: make any false or misleading statement as to the dividends or share of surplus previously paid on similar policies or annuity contracts

VI3-03.statement: Using a policy name or title that misrepresents the policy's true nature is prohibited.
VI3-03.quote: use any name or title of any policy or annuity contract or class of policies or annuity contracts misrepresenting the true nature thereof

VI3-04.statement: Rebating includes giving a client any part of the agent's, solicitor's or broker's commission as an inducement.
VI3-04.quote: any rebate of premiums or considerations payable on the contract or of any agent's, solicitor's or broker's commission relating thereto

VI3-05.statement: After a hearing, the commissioner may order a penalty of up to $1,000 per violation, or up to $5,000 per violation if the person knew or reasonably should have known it was a violation.
VI3-05.quote: the commissioner may order payment of a penalty not to exceed $1,000.00 for each and every act or violation unless the person knew or reasonably should have known he was in violation of this chapter, in which case the penalty shall be not more than $5,000.00 for every act or violation

VI3-06.statement: After finding a violation at a hearing, the commissioner issues an order to cease and desist.
VI3-06.quote: an order requiring such person to cease and desist from engaging in such method of competition, act or practice

VI3-07.statement: Before ordering a stop to a prohibited practice, the commissioner serves a statement of charges and notice of a hearing.
VI3-07.quote: he shall issue and serve upon such person a statement of the charges in that respect and a notice of a hearing thereon

VI3-30.statement: Before starting a life insurance sales presentation, the agent must say that he or she is acting as a life insurance agent and give the full name of the insurer represented.
VI3-30.quote: prior to commencing a life insurance sales presentation, that he or she is acting as a life insurance agent and the full name of the insurer the agent is representing

VI3-31.statement: A producer may not use titles like financial planner or investment advisor to imply an advisory business with compensation unrelated to sales unless that is actually the case.
VI3-31.quote: in such a way as to imply that he or she is primarily engaged in an advisory business in which compensation is unrelated to sales unless that is actually the case

VI3-40.statement: Failing to deliver a required Buyer's Guide, policy summary or illustration is an omission that misrepresents the policy and can bring Unfair Trade Practices Act penalties.
VI3-40.quote: shall constitute an omission that misrepresents the benefits, advantages, conditions or terms of an insurance policy

VI3-51.statement: If a policy is applied for as illustrated, a signed copy of the illustration goes to the insurer with the application, and a copy to the applicant.
VI3-51.quote: a copy of that illustration, signed in accordance with these rules, shall be submitted to the insurer at the time of policy application

VI3-52.statement: If the policy is issued other than as applied for, a 'Revised Illustration' must be sent with the policy and signed by the owner and producer no later than delivery.
VI3-52.quote: shall be labeled "Revised Illustration" and shall be signed and dated by the applicant or policy owner and producer

VI3-53.statement: If no illustration is used, the producer must certify that in writing on a form provided by the insurer.
VI3-53.quote: the producer or representative shall certify to that effect in writing on a form provided by the insurer

VI3-54.statement: Signed illustrations and certifications must be kept by the insurer until three years after the policy is no longer in force.
VI3-54.quote: shall be retained by the insurer until three years after the policy is no longer in force

VI4-01.statement: A policy, application, rider or endorsement delivered in New Jersey that does not comply with Title 17B is interpreted as if it did comply.
VI4-01.quote: shall be deemed to be in compliance with the requirements and shall be interpreted by the courts and among the persons affected by the policy or contract as if that policy or contract form were in compliance with the requirements

VI4-02.statement: A policy form filed with the commissioner is deemed approved 60 days after submission unless disapproved in writing within that time.
VI4-02.quote: shall be deemed approved upon the expiration of 60 days after the submission of the form unless disapproved in writing by the commissioner within that time

VI4-03.statement: Treating a noncomplying form as compliant does not relieve the insurer of any penalty for the violation.
VI4-03.quote: except that this provision shall not relieve the insurer from any penalty that may be imposed for violation of this act

VI4-04.statement: A policy on another person's life must benefit the insured, the insured's personal representative, or someone with an insurable interest when the contract was made.
VI4-04.quote: or to a person having, at the time when that contract was made, an insurable interest in the individual insured

VI4-05.statement: An individual has an insurable interest in a close relative by blood or by law in whom he has a substantial interest engendered by love and affection.
VI4-05.quote: (3) An individual has an insurable interest in the life, health and bodily safety of another individual to whom he is closely related by blood or by law and in whom he has a substantial interest engendered by love and affection.
